review.note:
Only one day of forecasts can be checked so far, and on that day they ran a little high, predicting a PSI of about 206 when the measured reading was 184, though still within the expected range. Even so, they were about twice as accurate as simply assuming the next day would match the latest reading. The most likely reason for the miss is a change in wind: by the day itself, less of Singapore's air was arriving from the big fire areas in Kalimantan and Sumatra and more from Java, where fires were smaller, so less smoke reached us even though Kalimantan's fires grew. One day is too little to justify changing the forecasts, so we are keeping them as they are and waiting for more results.

review.note: Over the last two scored days, our 1 to 3 day haze forecasts were off by about 17 PSI points on average, roughly half the error of simply assuming tomorrow will be like today, and the measured readings always fell within our forecast range. Today's reading of 227 was slightly above our central forecast of 219, and our forecasts have been running about 5 percent low overall. The most likely reason for this small miss is that fire activity in Kalimantan rose about five-fold after the forecast was issued, from about 7,800 to 37,600 MW. Over the same period, the share of air reaching Singapore from Kalimantan rose from about 57 percent to 79 percent. With only two days of results and no scores yet for forecasts 4 or more days ahead, it is too early to change anything, but this sharp rise in Kalimantan fires is worth watching closely.
